title: Early History of the Creek Indians and Their Neighbors: The Abihka
publisher: Smithsonian Institution, Bureau of American Ethnology
author: John R. Swanton
annotation: Bulletin 73 (1922), printed pp. 251–254; inspected the Abihka text and a public-domain scan of pp. 252–254. Compiles earlier records and named narrators; useful for conflicting etymologies and Abihkutci distinctions. Dated interpretations and historical descriptions need comparison with community accounts. Link opens the Smithsonian record and full PDF.

title: Source Material on the History and Ethnology of the Caddo Indians
publisher: Smithsonian Institution, Bureau of American Ethnology Bulletin 132; full-text transcription hosted by the Louisiana Anthology
author: John R. Swanton
annotation: 1942 sourcebook. Inspected selected Adai passages on printed pp. 13–15, 21–23, 75, and 84–85. Swanton compares discrepant population estimates, reports Caddo recollections, and warns that a later village called Adaise cannot securely be identified as Indigenous. Its historical synthesis and quoted records require source-specific reading. His assertion that Adai were entirely merged with other Caddo is a dated author's conclusion, not a verdict on today's communities or their identities.

title: A Dictionary of the Biloxi and Ofo Languages, Accompanied with Thirty-one Biloxi Texts and Numerous Biloxi Phrases
publisher: Smithsonian Institution, Bureau of American Ethnology, Bulletin 47
annotation: The foundational 1912 collection preserves Biloxi texts and vocabulary alongside a distinct Ofo dictionary. Reviewed the contents and Biloxi introduction, pp. 1–4, through the public-domain Wikisource transcription because the institutional PDF could not be fetched. The introduction explains editorial rearrangement and notation; this is not a full review of all texts.

title: The Classification and Distribution of the Pit River Indian Tribes of California
author: C. Hart Merriam
annotation: Published December 31, 1926, pp. 1–52. Read printed pp. 1–5, 12–14, 24–26, and selected name entries on pp. 41–47 in the full scan. Merriam acknowledges named Indigenous contributors and records variable names and contrasting environments. His narrower Fall River use of A-choo-mah-we and period classification require context; the map and taxonomy do not establish present jurisdiction or modern band membership. His salvage-era assumptions should not be repeated as statements about contemporary people.

title: Modern Square Grounds of the Creek Indians
author: John R. Swanton
annotation: Published November 11, 1931. Read introduction pp. 1–4 and Abihka pp. 13–15, including the author’s explanation of changed information. Documents Abihka/Talladega near Henryetta through dated fieldwork. This historical publication includes culturally sensitive ceremonial detail; its availability does not authorize reproducing practices or assuming current arrangements.

title: MS 2516 Alsea and Lower Umpqua texts and notes
